name: Dam safety hazard classification, inspection frequency, and owner obligations by US state
description: State-by-state comparison of dam safety programs: hazard classification systems, inspection frequencies, who must inspect, and dam owner obligations. Each record is one (state, hazard class) pair with the classification name, criteria for that class, required inspection interval, inspector qualifications, and whether inspections are mandatory or voluntary. Covers the ~91,000 non-federal dams in the US. Answers 'how often must my dam be inspected in [state]', 'what hazard classification is my dam', 'do I need a licensed engineer for inspections in [state]', and 'what are the penalties for non-compliance'. The ASDSO published a 50-state summary in 2020 as a PDF; it is now 6 years stale and not structured for search. This asset maintains the current state of each program from each state's own dam safety statute and program pages.
licence: US state government works — public domain

records.inspector_qualification: dam safety engineers
records.source_quote: Periodic inspections are conducted on existing "significant hazard" or "high hazard" dams — those located in areas where dam failure poses a risk for loss of life. The inspections are intended to identify deficiencies and to reasonably assure safe operation and confirm that maintenance is being adequately performed. Our dam safety engineers perform these inspections every five years.

records.inspector_qualification: professional engineer (PE) with experience in dams
records.source_quote: Chapter 31, Wis. Stats., requires owners of large dams to hire a professional engineer (PE) with experience in dams to inspect their dams periodically. The frequency of inspections completed by a professional engineer are related to the hazard rating of the dam: high hazard large dams – PE inspection every two years
